Document: Practice Direction 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot
Part 8 of 10
==================================================
[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] Defendant’s response on paper

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] 10.1(1) If the defendant wants to respond to the claim but is unable, for any reason, to do so online, the defendant must contact the court within 28 days after the date of issue of the claim form and confirm that they want to respond. For example, if the court issued the online claim form on 3rd March, the defendant would have to contact the court on or before 31st March. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] (1A) ) If at first the defendant had been able to respond online and had agreed more time to respond online under paragraph 5.1(3), but then became no longer able to respond online, the defendant may respond on paper instead, if the defendant contacts the court on time and tells the court that they still want to respond to the claim. The defendant contacts the court on time if they contact the court within 28 days after the date of issue of the claim form, or within such longer period up to an additional 28 days as agreed between the parties and notified to the court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] 10.1(2) The defendant may contact the court by telephone, using the HMCTS (as defined) helpline telephone number printed on the claim form. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] 10.1(3) If the defendant has confirmed to the court that they are unable (or no longer able) to use Online Civil Money Claims online, the court must send the defendant a paper copy of each of the following forms –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] (a) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] (b) Form N9A and N9B – Admission form and Defence and Counterclaim form (“paper response form”); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] (c) Form N180 or N181, to tell the court what requirements the defendant would have, should a court hearing be necessary. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.A1(1) This section applies only if the defendant is acting in person.] 10.1(4) When the court sends the paper copies of the forms to the defendant, it must also tell the defendant of the date that it sent out those forms. ## 10.1(5) The court must tell the claimant –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(5) The court must tell the claimant –] (a) if the defendant is unable (or no longer able) to use Online Civil Money Claims online

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(5) The court must tell the claimant –] (b) the date that it sent the paper forms to the defendant. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(5) The court must tell the claimant –] (5A) If the defendant has already been given more time under paragraph 5.1(3) to respond to the claim, the defendant must submit the completed paper response form within the agreed extended time. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(5) The court must tell the claimant –] 10.1(6) If a defendant has not already agreed with the claimant more time under paragraph 5.1(3) to respond to the claim, but would like more time, the defendant may agree with the claimant an extension of up to 28 days, and must notify the court of the agreed extension within the original 28 day period for responding to the claim. ## 10.1(7) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(7) Omitted] 10.1(8) The defendant must also submit to the court a completed paper response form which must be received by the court within the original 28 day period for responding to the claim, unless the defendant has already informed the court that the parties have agreed an extension of time to respond. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(7) Omitted] 10.1(9) If the parties have already agreed for more time, the defendant must still submit the completed paper response form on time so that the court receives the form within the agreed extended time.”

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(7) Omitted] (9A) At the same time that the defendant submits the completed paper response form, the defendant must also submit completed form N180 or N181 as appropriate to the court, to tell the court what requirements the defendant would have, should a court hearing be necessary. The requirement to submit form N180 or N181 as appropriate does not apply if the defendant’s response to the claim is to admit the whole of the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(7) Omitted] (9B) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.1(7) Omitted] 10.1(10) If the defendant does not submit the paper response form to the court on time, the claimant may apply to the court for default judgment and paragraph 11.1 will apply. ## Defendant’s response on paper – claim to be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Defendant’s response on paper – claim to be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims] 10.2(1) If the defendant responds on paper, the court must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the CNBC. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Defendant’s response on paper – claim to be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims] 10.2(2) The court must let the claimant and defendant know that the claim has been sent out of Online Civil Money Claims and explain why the claim has been sent out. ## 10.2(3) When the court sends the claim to the CNBC –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.2(3) When the court sends the claim to the CNBC –] (a) this practice direction will no longer apply to the claim; but

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10.2(3) When the court sends the claim to the CNBC –] (b) the rest of the Civil Procedure Rules and other practice directions will continue to apply with the following change: rule 26.4 (provisional allocation of a case to a case track in the court, and directions questionnaires) will apply as if the defendant filed the defence when the CNBC received the defendant’s paper response form from Online Civil Money Claims. ## SECTION 10A – Informing the court that the claim has been settled and discontinuance

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 10A – Informing the court that the claim has been settled and discontinuance] Informing the court that the claim has been settled

## 10A.1

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10A.1] (1) If the claim has been settled then, subject to sub-paragraph 10A.1(5) below, the claimant must use the OCMC website to tell the court that the claim has been settled, whereupon the proceedings must be stayed. The court must notify the defendant and tell them that they may contact the court, on time, to object. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10A.1] (2) The defendant contacts the court on time if they contact the court within 19 days after notification by the court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10A.1] (3) If the defendant objects on time, the court must transfer the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims to the “CNBC” (as defined) or where the parties have received an order from a judge or legal adviser at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, to that hearing centre. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10A.1] (4) A claimant must only notify the court of settlement under this Section if all matters in dispute are settled including who must pay the court fee and who must pay the costs of the proceedings. If there remains a dispute over the amount of costs then an application for an order can be made following the settlement to lift the stay and for the court to make an order to give effect to the settlement so far as it relates to costs. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10A.1] (Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10A.1] (5) If a party requires the terms of settlement to be incorporated into an order then (notwithstanding any notification in accordance with sub-paragraph 10A.1 (1) above) the claimant must make an application including the agreed form of order. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 10A.1] (Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

## Discontinuance

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] 10A.2-(1) ) In a claim not falling within subparagraph (3), if a claimant wishes to discontinue all or part of their claim, the claimant complies with CPR 38.3(1)(a) by filing the notice of discontinuance required by that rule—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (a) at the CNBC; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (b) where the parties have received an order from a judge or legal adviser at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, that hearing centre. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (2) If the claimant files a notice of discontinuance pursuant to  subparagraph (1), the claim must be transferred out of Online Civil  Money Claims to continue in the CNBC, or where the parties have  received an order from a judge or legal adviser at a County Court  hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, to continue in that hearing centre as  if it had been started under CPR Part 7. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (3) A claim falls within this subparagraph if—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (a) there are two parties and the claimant wishing to discontinue all or part of their claim is legally represented; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (b) there are more than two parties, and—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (i) where there are two claimants, each wishes to  discontinue their claim against the defendant to the same extent as the other; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (ii) where there is one claimant, they wish to discontinue their claim against both defendants to the same extent. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (4) Where the claim falls within subparagraph (3)—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (a) the claimant (or each claimant, if there are two) must  discontinue all or part of their claim by completing the relevant screens on the OCMC website in order to comply with CPR  38.3(1)(a) and (b), (2), (3) and (5);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (b) the effective date for the purposes of CPR 38.5(1) is the date the notification is sent via the OCMC website to the defendant (or defendants, if there are two) in accordance with paragraph  3.1(3) that the claimant has (or claimants have, if there are two) completed the relevant screens in accordance with paragraph (a) above. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Discontinuance] (5) If the claimant (or both claimants) discontinue all or part of their claim pursuant to subparagraph (4)(a), the claim will continue to remain within the OCMC system until a step can no longer be supported at which point it will be transferred out of the OCMC to continue in the CNBC, or where the parties have received an order from a judge or legal adviser at a County Court hearing centre, or have been informed that the claim is to be managed at a County Court hearing centre, to continue in that hearing centre as if it had been started under CPR Part 7. ## SECTION 11 – CONSEQUENCES OF THE DEFENDANT FAILING TO RESPOND ON TIME

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 11 – CONSEQUENCES OF THE DEFENDANT FAILING TO RESPOND ON TIME] Defendant acting in person – when default judgment cannot be made

## 11. (A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11. (A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person] Defendant acting in person – consequences of the defendant failing to respond to the court on time: judgment in default of responding

## 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] 11.1(1) If the defendant does not, on time, contact the court, submit a time extension form (if appropriate) and submit to the court a completed response form or a paper response form, the claimant may request that the court make a judgment in default unless subparagraph (2A) applies. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] 11.1(2) The claimant may request a judgment in default by completing and submitting form OCON205A (“judgment in default form”) online using the OCMC website. When requesting judgment, the claimant may also specify their repayment plan (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (2A) If there is a moratorium in place under the Debt Respite Scheme (Breathing Space Moratorium and Mental Health Crisis Moratorium) (England and Wales) Regulations 2020, so that a claimant needs the court’s permission to apply for a default judgment, the claimant must make an application to the court in accordance with Civil Procedure Rules Part 23. If the court receives such an application, it must send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (3) If the court receives a request for judgment in default, it must “enter judgment” (as defined), unless paragraph 11.1A applies (When default judgment cannot be made). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (4) If the claimant has specified a repayment plan in the request for judgment, the judgment must state that repayment is to be made in accordance with that repayment plan, unless, at the time the judgment is made, a repayment date specified in the repayment plan has passed. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (5) If a repayment date specified in the repayment plan has passed before the judgment is made, the judgment must still be made in accordance with that repayment plan, but –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (a) if the repayment plan states that the whole of the amount owed is to be paid by a date that has passed, the judgment must state that repayment must be made immediately;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (b) if the repayment plan states that the amount owed is to be paid by instalments and the date of the first instalment has passed, the judgment must state that the first instalment must be made by a date that is one calendar month after the date of the judgment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (6) If the claimant has not specified a repayment plan in the request for judgment, the judgment must state that the whole amount owed must be repaid in immediately. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (7) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (c) court fees and any fixed costs that the claimant is entitled to in accordance with Section 2B,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees or fixed fees, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] 11.1A (1) The claimant may not obtain a default judgment if, at the date judgment is to be entered, the defendant has satisfied the whole claim including any claim for costs. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (2) The claimant also may not obtain a default judgment under paragraph 11.1(3) if, at the date judgment is to be entered, the court has received any paper or electronic response from the defendant, or a notice or application from the defendant or another person. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1(1)(A1) This paragraph applies only when the defendant is acting in person.] (3) If the court has received any paper or electronic response, or notice or application, the claim must be referred to a judge for an order or directions

## 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (2) Unless sub-paragraph (8) applies, if the defendant does not respond to the claim by the time specified in paragraph 6A.2(1), or paragraph 6A.2(3) if relevant, the claimant may ask for judgment in default of a response to the claim by requesting judgment through the OCMC website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (3) A claimant requests judgment through the OCMC website by –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (a) completing the relevant screens on the website; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (b) submitting the completed screens using the website. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (4)  Judgment is to be entered following a request made under subparagraph (3) if at the date of making the request –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (a)  the defendant has not responded to the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (b) the defendant has not applied to strike out the claim, or, if the defendant has applied to strike out the claim, that application has been disposed of;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (c) no party has applied for summary judgment under Civil Procedure Rules Part 24, or, if any party has applied for summary judgment under Part 24, that application has been disposed of; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (d) the defendant has not satisfied the whole claim, including costs. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (5) If the claimant has specified a repayment plan in the request for judgment, the judgment must state that repayment must be made in accordance with that repayment plan. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (6) If the claimant has not specified a repayment plan in the request for judgment, the judgment must state that the whole amount owed must be paid in immediately. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (7) The judgment will be made for the amount of –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (a) the claim;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (b) any interest that the claimant is entitled to and has claimed on the claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (c) court fees and any fixed costs that the claimant is entitled to in accordance with Section 2B,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] minus any payments of the amount owed on the claim form that the defendant has already paid. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (If a claimant wants to claim any costs other than court fees or fixed costs, for example the costs of paying for expert evidence, the claimant would have to  make an application. Section 16B contains provisions about making  applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (8) If the defendant does not respond to the claim by the time specified in paragraph 6A.2(1) or 6A.2(3) if relevant and –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (a) CPR rule 12.11 would apply if the claim had been started under Civil Procedure Rule Part 7; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (b) there is a moratorium in place under the Debt Respite Scheme (Breathing Space Moratorium and Mental Health Crisis Moratorium) (England and Wales) Regulations 2020,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] the claimant may not request judgment in default through the OCMC website but may instead make an application for default judgment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] (Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.1B (1)This paragraph applies only when the defendant is legally represented.] What happens when the defendant does not respond, and the claimant does not take further action against the defendant, for 6 months

## 11.2 If 6 months have passed since the court issued the claim and in that time –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.2 If 6 months have passed since the court issued the claim and in that time –] (a) the defendant has not responded to the claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.2 If 6 months have passed since the court issued the claim and in that time –] (b) the claimant has not applied for a default judgment or summary judgment, the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.2 If 6 months have passed since the court issued the claim and in that time –] Parties acting in person – what happens where there has been no action on a claim for 6 months

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 11.2 If 6 months have passed since the court issued the claim and in that time –] 12.1 If the parties are acting in person and no steps have been taken on a claim by either the claimant or the defendant for 6 months, the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). ## Confirming that the contents of claims, defences and paper defences are true (statement of truth)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Confirming that the contents of claims, defences and paper defences are true (statement of truth)] 13.1-(1) When the claimant or the claimant’s legal representative submits a claim , the claim must include the following statement of truth signed or otherwise verified by the claimant or their legal representative:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Confirming that the contents of claims, defences and paper defences are true (statement of truth)] “[I believe] [The claimant believes] that the facts stated in this claim are true. [I understand] [The claimant understands] that proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against anyone who makes, or causes to be made, a false statement in a document verified by a statement of truth without an honest belief in its truth.”

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Confirming that the contents of claims, defences and paper defences are true (statement of truth)] (2) When the defendant or the defendant’s legal representative submits a defence or paper defence (as appropriate), the defence must include the following statement of truth signed or otherwise verified by the defendant or their legal representative: “[I believe] [The defendant believes] that the facts stated in this defence are true. [I understand] [The defendant understands] that proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against anyone who makes, or causes to be made, a false statement in a document verified by a statement of truth without an honest belief in its truth.”

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Confirming that the contents of claims, defences and paper defences are true (statement of truth)] Submitting documents at court– timing of submitting

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Confirming that the contents of claims, defences and paper defences are true (statement of truth)] 14.1(A1) For the purposes of this practice direction, a form, document or email submitted to the court electronically is received by the court when it is recorded as received by the OCMC website, or as appropriate by HMCTS email software. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Confirming that the contents of claims, defences and paper defences are true (statement of truth)] 14.1(A2) If the OCMC website is functioning normally so that it can receive forms and documents, and the court receives a form or document before 4.00 p.m., that form or document is treated as submitted that day. The same rule applies in relation to emails received by the court before 4.00 p.m. where the HMCTS email software is functioning normally. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Confirming that the contents of claims, defences and paper defences are true (statement of truth)] 14.1(1) If the OCMC website is functioning normally so that it can receive forms and documents, and the court receives a form or document at or after 4.00 p.m. and before or at 11.59 p.m., that form or document is treated as submitted before 4.00 p.m. on the next day the court office is open. The same rule applies in relation to emails received by the court at or after 4.00 p.m. and before or at 11.59 p.m., where the HMCTS email software is functioning normally. ## 14.1(2) If –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (a) the OCMC website is malfunctioning and cannot receive forms and/or documents, or the HMCTS email software is malfunctioning so that it cannot receive emails;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (b) that malfunction starts before but continues up to or beyond 4.00 p.m. on a particular day; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (c) that malfunction alone prevents a person from being able to submit a form, document or email (as appropriate) within a time limit imposed by this practice direction or in “directions” (as defined),

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (2A) Where a paper form or document is received  at the OCMC postal address or OCMC email  address before 4.00 p.m., that document is treated as submitted to the court that day. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 14.1(2) If –] (2B) Where a paper form or document is received  at the OCMC postal address or OCMC email address at or after 4.00 p.m. and before or at 11.59 p.m., that document is treated as submitted to the court before 4.00 p.m.
